nodes.name: M1 Run (webhook)
nodes.notes: Entry point. Body: {registrants_csv_url?, event_slug, skip_clay?}. Responds via 'Respond Run Started' AFTER 'Call Module API - Prepare' returns, not on receipt -- so a reviewer's curl gets back the real run_id, not just an ack.

nodes.name: Call Module API - Prepare

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { module: "m1", phase: "prepare", live: true, inputs: { registrants_csv_url: $json.body.registrants_csv_url, event_slug: $json.body.event_slug } } }}

nodes.notes: Module API /run, phase=prepare. timeout=1800000ms (1800s) per spec. retryOnFail=false deliberately: prepare does dedupe + LLM inference + writes interim state, so a blind retry on a slow-but-succeeding call risks a duplicate run rather than a clean failure. Auth is a bearer header built from $env.MODULE_API_TOKEN, not an n8n credential -- module API has no per-request credential, just the shared token.

nodes.name: Prepare OK?
nodes.notes: True = prepare's JSON body has ok:true (HTTP 200 either way per module-api.md -- app-level failure is still HTTP 200 with ok:false). False routes to 'Stop: Prepare Failed' so the execution shows red with the API's own error string, per the no-silent-failure design rule.

nodes.name: Stop: Prepare Failed

parameters.errorMessage: =m1 prepare failed for event {{ $('M1 Run (webhook)').item.json.body.event_slug }}: {{ $json.error || 'module API returned ok:false with no error message' }}

nodes.notes: Terminal failure node -- same pattern as v1's 'Stop with Clear Error'. Surfaces the module API's own error string in the execution log.

nodes.name: Respond Run Started
nodes.notes: Fires only after prepare succeeds, so the reviewer's curl gets the real run_id. Execution keeps running after this node (Respond to Webhook does not terminate the workflow) -- the Clay leg and finalize continue in the background.

nodes.name: Skip Clay?

conditions.leftValue: ={{ ($('Call Module API - Prepare').item.json.next && $('Call Module API - Prepare').item.json.next.clay_domains || []).length }}

nodes.notes: True (skip) = caller passed skip_clay:true OR prepare returned no clay_domains -- jump straight to finalize with clay_results:{}. False = at least one domain needs Clay enrichment.

nodes.name: Build Finalize Body (No Clay)

parameters.jsCode:
const runId = $('Call Module API - Prepare').item.json.run_id;
return [{ json: { run_id: runId, clay_results: {} } }];

nodes.notes: No-Clay path body for the finalize call. Same output shape as 'Assemble Clay Results' below so both branches can feed 'Call Module API - Finalize' directly without a merge node.

nodes.name: Split Domains to Items
nodes.notes: One item per domain still missing/low-confidence firmographics. 'Skip Clay?' already guarantees this list is non-empty on this branch.

nodes.name: Push Domain to Clay
nodes.notes: Fires once per domain (n8n loops an httpRequest node over each input item automatically). Clay's table-level HTTP-API enrichment column reads {domain, run_id} off the row and later posts the enriched result back to callback_url. continueOnFail is left at its default (false/stop) -- a failed push should show red, not vanish silently. retryOnFail covers transient network faults only.

nodes.name: Wait for Clay Enrichment (10 min)
nodes.notes: TIME-BASED wait, not webhook-resume -- see 'Sticky Note: Why Not Wait-Webhook-Resume'. Gives Clay up to 10 minutes to enrich and call every domain back; whatever has landed in the static-data accumulator by then is what ships to finalize.

nodes.name: Assemble Clay Results
nodes.notes: Reads whatever 'Accumulate Clay Result' wrote into workflow static data for this run_id, fills any domain that never called back with null (finalize's phase='finalize' logic already treats missing clay data as 'fall back to LLM/rules' per module-api.md precedence). Clears the accumulator entry afterward so static data doesn't grow unbounded across runs.

nodes.name: Call Module API - Finalize
nodes.notes: Module API /run, phase=finalize. Fed by either 'Build Finalize Body (No Clay)' or 'Assemble Clay Results' -- both emit {run_id, clay_results}. retryOnFail=false: finalize pushes to HubSpot, so a blind retry could double-upsert. Response includes the HubSpot push receipt artifact URL per spec.

nodes.name: Finalize OK?
nodes.notes: Same ok:true gate as 'Prepare OK?', on the finalize response.

nodes.name: Stop: Finalize Failed

parameters.errorMessage: =m1 finalize failed for run {{ $('Call Module API - Prepare').item.json.run_id }}: {{ $json.error || 'module API returned ok:false with no error message' }}

nodes.notes: Terminal failure node for a finalize-side failure (e.g. HubSpot push rejected).

nodes.name: Build Evidence Summary
nodes.notes: input_rows/output_rows/hubspot_matches/llm_calls come from prepare's summary (per module-api.md's shown example); contacts_upserted/verified_*_pct are assumed to live in finalize's summary since module-api.md doesn't show a finalize response example -- verify field names against a live finalize call and adjust if they differ. clay_domains_sent/returned are read defensively via try/catch since 'Assemble Clay Results' never executes on the no-clay branch.

nodes.name: Write Run Summary to Disk
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED against a live instance -- flagging per this skill's own audit rule. The brief named this a 'Write Binary File node'; n8n's dedicated Write Binary File node is deprecated/removed in current 1.x/2.x, folded into 'Read/Write Files from Disk' (n8n-nodes-base.readWriteFile, operation=write). Reads the binary property built by 'Build Evidence Summary' and writes it to /home/node/.n8n/runs/<run_id>.json inside the container -- confirm the parameter names (fileName, dataPropertyName) against your instance's node panel before relying on this in production.

nodes.name: Run Summary (Final)
nodes.notes: Re-emits the clean evidence summary (no binary payload) as the workflow's last node, so the n8n execution log shows the full receipt object per the spec's requirement.

nodes.name: Clay Result Callback (webhook)
nodes.notes: Separate always-on trigger, NOT the Wait node's own resume webhook. Clay's HTTP-API enrichment column posts here once per row (once per domain) -- see the accumulator sticky note for why a Wait-node webhook-resume can't be used for this instead.

nodes.name: Accumulate Clay Result
nodes.notes: Writes into $getWorkflowStaticData('global'), which n8n persists on the WORKFLOW (shared across all executions of this workflow, not per-execution) -- this is what lets N independent Clay callbacks accumulate somewhere the main execution's 'Assemble Clay Results' node can read back after its time-based Wait elapses.

parameters.content:
## WHY THIS ISN'T A WAIT-NODE WEBHOOK RESUME
v1's Wait node used resume:webhook and relied on Clay's TABLE-LEVEL 'run complete' trigger posting once with every row bundled ({rows:[...]})  -- that only works because it is a single POST.

This brief's Clay leg pushes ONE ROW AT A TIME and expects Clay's HTTP-API COLUMN to call back once PER ROW. A Wait node in resume:webhook mode resumes on the FIRST POST to its resume URL and tears the webhook down -- callbacks 2..N for the other domains would arrive at a dead URL and be lost.

Fix: 'Wait for Clay Enrichment (10 min)' uses resume:timeInterval instead (a plain timer, not tied to any webhook), and a SEPARATE always-on webhook ('Clay Result Callback (webhook)') collects every per-domain callback into $getWorkflowStaticData('global'), keyed by run_id. 'Assemble Clay Results' reads that accumulator once the timer elapses. This is the standard n8n pattern for 'collect N async callbacks then continue' -- workflow static data is shared across executions of the same workflow.

## ENV VARS (no n8n credentials needed)
MODULE_API_URL, MODULE_API_TOKEN, CLAY_WEBHOOK_URL, WEBHOOK_URL -- all read via $env, so self-hosted n8n needs N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false or every $env reference in this workflow (including inside httpRequest URL/body fields) resolves to nothing.

No HubSpot/Clay credential objects are referenced anywhere in this file -- the module API holds the HubSpot token server-side, and Clay auth is just an unguessable table-webhook URL.
